Senses.Explanation: A life-root is the hold that Chan records locate and describe as cut, broken, or gathered up. The phrase occurs 829 times in 226 allowlisted texts. Luyuan spreads his hand and says that the life-roots of all the old masters and senior monks are 'all here' (天下老和尚．諸上座命根。總在這裏). Jiaozhong Huian Miguang supplies the corpus's clearest physical comparison: one cut at a tree's root severs its life-root, whereas chopping its branches does not (如人斫樹，根下一刀，則命根斷矣。汝向枝上斫，其能斷命根乎). Ying'an Tanhua's record says that when a blind was rolled up, 'the lacquer bucket broke open and the life-root snapped on the spot' (豁然漆桶破，命根嚗地斷). Wuyi Yuanlai postpones speech until the questioner's own life-root is severed (待闍黎命根斷即道). These predicates make the life-root a locatable and severable Chan expression, distinct from the enumerated vital faculty in the second sense; the entry makes no claim about an inward meaning beyond those recorded predicates.
Senses.Note: Common forms include 'the life-root is not severed' and 'sever the life-root.' Gaofeng Yuanmiao's repeatedly cited question is, 'A completely broken-through person is originally free of birth and death; why is the life-root not severed?' (大徹底人本脫生死，因什命根不斷).

Occurrences.Kwic: 天下老和尚．諸上座命根。總在這裏。有僧出曰。還收得也無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), in Luyuan's section, identifies Luyuan as the exact speaker who says that the old masters' and senior monks' life-roots are all here.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如人斫樹，根下一刀，則命根斷矣。汝向枝上斫，其能斷命根乎？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Orthodox Continuation of the Lamp (續燈正統), in Jiaozhong Huian Miguang's section, identifies Huian Miguang as the exact speaker of the root-and-branches comparison.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一日見卷簾，豁然漆桶破，命根嚗地斷，便說箇頌子
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Ying'an Tanhua (應菴曇華禪師語錄) identifies Ying'an Tanhua as the exact record owner and verse speaker who says that the life-root snapped on the spot.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：待闍黎命根斷即道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Wuyi Yuanlai (無異元來禪師廣錄), exact response turn in a complete public interview: Wuyi Yuanlai tells the unnamed questioner that he will speak when the questioner's life-root is severed. The mixed two-speaker KWIC was narrowed to Wuyi's actor-pure turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 大徹底人本脫生死，因什命根不斷？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Hanyue Fazang (三峰藏和尚語錄) explicitly quotes Gaofeng Yuanmiao's question about why the life-root remains unsevered; Gaofeng is the exact quoted speaker and Hanyue Fazang the later recorder.

Occurrences.Kwic: 參禪別無奇特，祇要當人命根斷，疑情脫，千眼頓開
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), in Baohua Pujian's section, identifies Baohua Pujian as the exact speaker who says that Chan study requires the person's life-root to be severed.

Senses.Explanation: In enumerative prose, the same graphs name the vital faculty as one faculty among others. Yongming Yanshou says, 'Among the faculties, the vital faculty is foremost' (諸根中，命根為最). This is a different referent from the Chan idiom that masters locate, seize, and sever, so it is retained separately rather than blurred into that usage.
Senses.Note: This sense is included because it is attested within the allowlisted record, not because a Buddhist glossary controls the Chan sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如諸根中。命根為最。佛正法正行中。此心為最。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Record of the Source-Mirror (宗鏡錄) identifies Yongming Yanshou as the authorial speaker who calls the vital faculty foremost among the faculties.
